name: Fig
grown_as: 'Brown Turkey', the hardiest common fig in the UK, kept small in a large pot or with its roots restricted in a sunny spot. It sets fruit without pollination (there is no fig wasp in Britain).
habit: A deciduous, many-stemmed shrub or small tree, 2 to 4 m, spreading wider than tall, with thick, stubby, smooth grey branches. Every part bleeds white milky sap when cut. Often seen wild on walls and riverbanks in British towns.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate, crowded towards the shoot tips
leaf.outline: Large, 10 to 25 cm long and about as wide, cut into three to five (sometimes seven) deep lobes like a spread hand; the lobes widen towards their blunt, rounded ends and are separated by rounded gaps (sinuses)
leaf.base: Heart-shaped, the two lower lobes curving back towards the stalk
leaf.tip: Each lobe blunt or broadly rounded; the middle lobe the longest
leaf.margin: Wavy, with irregular shallow blunt teeth, mostly towards the lobe ends
leaf.veins: Three to five main veins fanning from the top of the stalk, one running into each lobe, pale yellow-green and raised beneath, with a net of smaller veins between
leaf.surface: Thick and rough like fine sandpaper above (short stiff hairs); paler and softly hairy beneath
leaf.colour: Mid to dark green, often with a grey cast above; pale yellow-green veins; butter yellow in autumn

flower.form: Never seen from outside: hundreds of tiny flowers line the inside of a hollow, fleshy, pear-shaped case (the young fig, a syconium). Only a cut fig shows them
flower.petals: None that show; each tiny female flower is a little stalked knob with a thread-like style pointing inwards
flower.colour: Cream to pink inside, ripening to deep pink-red; the outer skin green
flower.centre: A hollow middle; at the top a small opening (the eye) closed by overlapping tiny scales
flower.behind: Three small green bracts where the fig joins its short stalk
flower.carried: Singly in the angle between leaf stalk and shoot, held upright or angled out
flower.size: The young fig 1 to 3 cm; each flower about 2 mm
flower.season: Through the summer; in Britain the figs that ripen are the pea-sized ones formed at the shoot tips the summer before

fruit: The whole fig swells into a pear- or top-shaped fruit, 4 to 7 cm, narrowing to a short stalk, with the eye at the broad end. 'Brown Turkey' ripens purple-brown, the skin sometimes splitting; inside, soft red-pink flesh full of tiny seeds. Ripe figs droop on their stalks. August to September. Fruit set: small hard green figs in the leaf angles, upright.
seedling: Not drawn: grown from cuttings or bought plants
winter: Bare, thick, smooth grey branches with a pointed green-brown bud at each tip, often with small pea-sized embryo figs just below it; large pale leaf scars.

leaf: three to five deep lobes like a spread hand, widening to blunt rounded ends
main veins fanning from the stalk, one into each lobe
wavy edge with blunt teeth, not sharp ones
bloom: a fig cut in half lengthways, the hollow inside lined with many tiny flowers pointing inwards
the eye at the broad end
young: a few very large deeply lobed leaves on stout stalks
dormant: pointed tip buds with small embryo figs below them
growing: large hand-shaped lobed leaves crowded at the shoot tips
set: small green figs held upright where the leaf stalks meet the shoot
crop: pear-shaped purple-brown figs drooping on short stalks from the leaf angles

look_alikes: Plane and sycamore leaves are thinner and smooth with pointed lobes and sharp teeth; neither tree bears figs. Mulberry has some lobed leaves but the fruit is a blackberry-like cluster.
